an9.38:1.1: Then two brahman cosmologists [Ājīvakas] went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, exchanged courteous greetings with him.
an9.38:1.2: After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, they sat to one side. As they were sitting there, they said to the Blessed One,
an9.38:2.1: “Master Gotama, Pūraṇa Kassapa—all-knowing, all-seeing—claims exhaustive knowledge & vision:
an9.38:2.2: ‘Whether I am standing or walking, awake or asleep, continual, unflagging knowledge & vision is established within me.’
an9.38:2.4: ‘I dwell with infinite knowledge, knowing & seeing the finite cosmos.’
an9.38:2.5: Yet Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta—all-knowing, all-seeing—also claims exhaustive knowledge & vision:
an9.38:2.6: ‘Whether I am standing or walking, awake or asleep, continual, unflagging knowledge & vision is established within me.’
an9.38:2.8: ‘I dwell with infinite knowledge, knowing & seeing the infinite cosmos.’
an9.38:2.9: Of these two speakers of knowledge, these two who contradict each other, which is telling the truth, and which is lying?”
an9.38:3.4: I will teach you the Dhamma.
an9.38:3.5: Listen and pay close attention. I will speak.”
an9.38:3.6: “Yes, sir,” the brahmans responded to the Blessed One,
an9.38:4.1: “Suppose that there were four men standing at the four directions, endowed with supreme speed & stride.
an9.38:4.2: Like that of a strong archer—well-trained, a practiced hand, a practiced sharp-shooter—shooting a light arrow across the shadow of a palm tree: Such would be the speed with which they were endowed.
an9.38:4.3: As far as the east sea is from the west: Such would be the stride with which they were endowed.
an9.38:4.4: Then the man standing at the eastern direction would say,
an9.38:4.5: ‘I, by walking, will reach the end [or: edge (anta)] of the cosmos.’
an9.38:4.6: He—with a one-hundred year life, a one-hundred year span—would spend one hundred years traveling—apart from the time spent on eating, drinking, chewing & tasting, urinating & defecating, and sleeping to fight off weariness—but without reaching the end of the cosmos he would die along the way.
an9.38:4.7: [Similarly with the men standing at the western, southern, & northern directions.]
an9.38:4.13: I tell you, it isn’t through that sort of traveling that the end of the cosmos is known, seen, or reached.
an9.38:4.14: But at the same time, I tell you that there is no making an end of suffering & stress without reaching the end of the cosmos.
an9.38:5.1: “These five strings of sensuality are, in the discipline of the noble ones, called the cosmos.
an9.38:5.3: Forms cognizable via the eye—agreeable, pleasing, charming, endearing, enticing, linked to sensual desire;
an9.38:5.7: tactile sensations cognizable via the body—agreeable, pleasing, charming, endearing, enticing, linked to sensual desire.
an9.38:5.8: These are the five strings of sensuality that, in the discipline of the noble ones, are called the cosmos.
an9.38:6.1: “There is the case where a monk—quite secluded from sensuality, secluded from unskillful qualities—enters & remains in the first jhāna: rapture & pleasure born of seclusion, accompanied by directed thought & evaluation.
an9.38:6.2: This is called a monk who, coming to the end of the cosmos, remains at the end of the cosmos.
an9.38:6.4: ‘He is encompassed in the cosmos; he has not escaped from the cosmos.’
an9.38:6.5: And I too say of him,
an9.38:6.6: ‘He is encompassed in the cosmos; he has not escaped from the cosmos.’
an9.38:7.1: [Similarly with the second, third, & fourth jhānas, and with the attainment of the dimensions of the infinitude of space, the infinitude of consciousness, nothingness, and neither perception nor non-perception.]
an9.38:10.1: “And further, with the complete transcending of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, he enters & remains in the cessation of perception & feeling. And as he sees (that) with discernment, effluents are completely ended.
an9.38:10.2: This is called a monk who, coming to the end of the cosmos, remains at the end of the cosmos, having crossed over attachment in the cosmos.”
